stack balance: at L648080 the outstanding stack (assuming callees 0x0070ED80/0x0043A550 pop their single args, forced by body 1's fixed epilogues - see RDER-P12-07) is exactly [saved ESI][return address]; a working RET therefore requires exactly one more pop before RET; the tail CANNOT be e.g. two pops (would unbalance) or zero pops (RET would return to saved ESI)
rederivations.independent_check: forcing argument re-derived independently and confirmed: the tail is constrained to consume exactly [saved ESI][ret]. HOWEVER the forcing constrains the stack effect, not the opcodes: an unread tail row could still write EAX (e.g. MOV EAX,imm) between the final pop and RET while consuming the same slots... actually no: only ONE stack slot may be consumed (saved ESI) plus the RET pop; any EAX-writer without stack effect would still fit (e.g. 'POP ESI; MOV EAX,x; RET' or 'MOV EAX,x; POP ESI; RET'). Therefore EAX-preservation at body 2's RET is NOT in-window provable -> STRONGLY_SUPPORTED (not CONFIRMED) is the correct grade. Worker's countermodel in P12-C2 states exactly this.
rederivations.verdict: CONFIRMED (grading correctness); body 2 return stands as STRONGLY_SUPPORTED
